main_text.l: Nomine tum Grajo ceu littera proxima prima
Pangitur in cerâ doêli mucrone magistri.
Sic & humi pingui ferrata cuspidû illâ
Deprimitur, folio viridis, pede candida Beta.
main_text.head: LITTERARUM. EPISTOLARUM. TABULARUM.
main_text.p: TABULAS obsignabant, præsertim amantes imagine suâ: & annulis signatorijs.
Signum autem annuli imprimebatur in ceram. Dehinc in Epistolarum usum successit creta.

p.i: Hæc quæ est ànobis prolata laudatio, obsignata erat cretâ illâ Asiaticâ, quæ est ferè omnibus nota nobis.

main_text.p: Nec procul abluduntunt illa S. Leonrij lib. v. contra Judæos:
Greek passage, a quotation from Leontius, printed in Greek letters, with the Latin sentence: Quem locum ideò adscripsi, q- rarior author, & non in omnium manibus.
ANTEQUAM litteras recitarent, jubebant, adversus quos facerent, ne postea dicerent fictas, cognoscere signum. Bacch. 4. 6. v. 19. Pseud. 4. 2. v. 45. Vide P. Victorium lib. 14. cap. 4.

page.notes: The Greek passage is printed in Greek letters and is not reliably legible here; it is given only in outline. Marks such as "q;" and "ꝑ" are as printed. Several Latin words in the italic verse lines and the Greek are doubtful.
